question: What is capital expenditure?

options.text: Amount spent on subsidy for farmers

solution:
The correct answer is __**Amount spent on infrastructure development**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Capital expenditure** refers to the amount spent by an organization or government on acquiring, maintaining, or improving fixed assets such as buildings, vehicles, equipment, or land.
 
• It is considered an investment in the long-term assets of the organization or country, which will provide benefits over several years.
 
• Examples of capital expenditure include spending on **infrastructure development, purchasing machinery, upgrading technology,** and constructing new facilities.
 
• Such expenditures are essential for the growth and development of both public and private sectors, as they enhance the productive capacity and efficiency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Capital expenditure is different from **operational expenditure** (OpEx), which refers to the costs required for the day-to-day functioning of an organization, such as salaries, utilities, and rent.
 
• Capital expenditures are usually recorded as assets on the balance sheet, while operational expenditures are recorded as expenses on the income statement.
 
• Effective management of capital expenditure is crucial for long-term financial planning and sustainability.
 
• Governments often allocate a significant portion of their budgets to capital expenditures to promote economic growth and improve public services.
